xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3671: Test-home OVERDECK_HOME poisoned shared tmux global env — every conversation spawn falsely reports 'Spawn failed'

plan.title: Test-home OVERDECK_HOME poisoned shared tmux global env — every conversation spawn falsely reports 'Spawn failed' (supervisor socket bound in /tmp test home)
plan.author: agent:claude

narratives.Problem: A throwaway test dashboard running with OVERDECK_HOME=/tmp on the shared managed tmux socket stamped its home into the server's global env via the PAN-1798 sanitizer. Every PTY supervisor then resolved getOverdeckHome() from that polluted env and bound its socket under the dead /tmp home, so the real dashboard's 30s socket wait timed out and recorded fork_status='failed' / spawn_error / markConversationEnded on conversations that were alive and working. The lifecycle heal resurrected status but never cleared the failure fields, no operator door existed to clear them, and the timeout error quoted a healthy harness statusline as the 'supervisor output' failure.
narratives.Proposal: Four independent fixes plus heal, door, and docs: (1) the sanitizer pins canonical HOME/OVERDECK_HOME (from os.homedir()) on the default managed socket — always, never the caller's env — and warns when a non-canonical-home process uses the shared socket; custom sockets keep caller-env pinning. (2) Every non-remote launcher script exports OVERDECK_HOME from the spawning process's resolved home. (3) A supervisor-socket timeout with a live tmux session degrades to a warn-log + fallback delivery instead of recording spawn/fork failure; extractSupervisorFailure returns null on a healthy pane so the error says 'no error output' instead of quoting the statusline. (4) markConversationRunning clears spawn_error always and fork_status/fork_error when 'failed', so both heal sites self-repair. (5) New operator door POST /api/conversations/:name/clear-fork-state guarded on session liveness, plus `pan conversations heal <name>`. (6) docs/AGENT-MESSAGE-DELIVERY.md documents the invariant, degrade, and door. PRD: .pan/drafts/PAN-3671.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Janitor sweep of 619 stale pty-conv-*.sock files (separate concern per the issue; file a sibling issue)
- Mechanically forcing test/throwaway dashboards onto their own tmux socket (warning advises OVERDECK_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME instead)
- Frontend changes to ConversationPanel.tsx (clearing spawn_error fixes the 'Failed to start' screen)
- Changing the delivery fallback ordering (supervisor → channels → tmux-paste)
- Healing rows whose tmux session is genuinely dead (their failure state is truthful)
- Retroactive repair of tonight's already-cleared rows beyond the heal and the operator door

autoDecisions.summary: Sanitizer refusal + canonical pinning instead of forcing test dashboards onto their own socket
autoDecisions.rationale: No mechanical test-dashboard launch path exists to enforce socket isolation (the PAN-3668 dashboard was launched ad hoc); pinning canonical values on the shared socket is always safe and repairs pollution from any clean-env process.

autoDecisions.summary: Heal implemented inside markConversationRunning rather than at each heal site
autoDecisions.rationale: Both heal sites (conversation-lifecycle.ts:172, conversation-list.ts:111) call this one writer; one change fixes both and preserves the single write door.

autoDecisions.summary: Heal clears fork_status only when 'failed'; in-flight fork states preserved
autoDecisions.rationale: getStuckForks() recovery keys off fork_status NOT NULL AND != 'failed'; clearing 'spawning'/'injecting' would orphan fork-request recovery.

autoDecisions.summary: Degrade keeps delivery_method='auto' rather than storing a forced fallback
autoDecisions.rationale: deliverAgentMessage already falls back supervisor → channels → tmux-paste at delivery time; no stored state change is needed for delivery to work.

autoDecisions.summary: Operator door is REST endpoint + thin CLI client, no direct-DB CLI
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches the pan conversations move pattern (resolve locally, POST to dashboard) and the single write door tenet.

autoDecisions.summary: Stale socket janitor sweep deferred to a sibling issue
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue body itself calls it 'a separate concern'; it is a one-line hygiene fix unrelated to the failure chain.

items.title: Sanitizer pins canonical HOME/OVERDECK_HOME on the default managed socket

expected_outputs: sanitizer test cases pass: /tmp caller home never stamped on default socket, unset vars still pinned, custom socket keeps caller home

narrative.Action: Add getCanonicalOverdeckHome() to src/lib/paths.ts (join(homedir(), '.overdeck')). Rewrite sanitizeManagedServerGlobalEnvSync in src/lib/tmux.ts (currently lines 233-253): on the default managed socket (OVERDECK_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME unset) pin HOME=homedir() and OVERDECK_HOME=getCanonicalOverdeckHome() ALWAYS (remove the `if (!value) continue` skip), never the caller's env; when getOverdeckHome() differs from canonical on the default socket, console.warn advising OVERDECK_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME. On a custom socket keep pinning the caller's resolved values (cleanEnv.HOME ?? homedir(), getOverdeckHome()). Update the PAN-1798 doc comment above the function. Export the sanitizer for tests via the @internal pattern (precedent: _resetWarnedManagedServerDirtyForTest, tmux.ts:260). Exact before/after snippets are in PRD WI-1 (.pan/drafts/PAN-3671.md). Tests (mock execFileSync): (a) OVERDECK_HOME=/tmp/fake on default socket → canonical pinned, /tmp never stamped, warning logged; (b) caller env lacking HOME/OVERDECK_HOME → both still pinned; (c) OVERDECK_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME=custom + /tmp home → caller home pinned on custom socket.

items.title: Given caller env OVERDECK_HOME=/tmp/fake on the default socket, when the sanitizer runs, then set-environment -g receives the canonical home and never /tmp/fake, and a warning is logged naming the non-canonical home
Given a caller env lacking HOME and OVERDECK_HOME, the sanitizer still pins both canonical values (repair path; no skip-on-unset)
Given OVERDECK_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME=custom and OVERDECK_HOME=/tmp/fake, the sanitizer pins the caller's home on the custom socket (isolation preserved)

Supervisor-socket timeout with live tmux session degrades to fallback delivery instead of recording failure

expected_outputs: degrade tests pass: live-session timeout resolves without failure writes; dead-session timeout propagates

narrative.Action: In spawnConversationSession (src/lib/overdeck/conversation-runtime.ts), wrap the `await waitForPtySupervisorSocket(tmuxSession)` call (lines 804-806) in try/catch: on error, if `await tmuxSessionExists(tmuxSession)` (already defined at line 292) then console.warn a '[conversations] PTY supervisor socket unavailable … continuing with fallback delivery' message carrying the original error text and CONTINUE; otherwise rethrow. Exact snippet in PRD WI-3. This covers both the create path (handleConversationCreate catch at lines 945-954) and the fork path (handleForkPipelineFailure, conversation-forks.ts:400-405) because both flow through spawnConversationSession. New test tests/unit/lib/overdeck/conversation-runtime-supervisor-degrade.test.ts mocking the socket stat and tmuxSessionExists, using vi.useFakeTimers() for the 30s PTY_SUPERVISOR_SOCKET_WAIT_MS wait: (a) timeout + session alive → spawn resolves, updateSpawnError/updateForkStatus/markConversationEnded never called, warn logged; (b) timeout + session gone → error propagates and existing failure recording fires.

extractSupervisorFailure returns null on a healthy pane; timeout error stops quoting the statusline as failure output

expected_outputs: failure-message tests pass: healthy pane → null + 'no error output' message; error pane → error lines

narrative.Action: In src/lib/overdeck/conversation-runtime.ts change extractSupervisorFailure (lines 416-422): when no error-shaped lines match, return null instead of falling back to the last 3 pane lines. Then in waitForPtySupervisorSocket (lines 435-439), when the extract returns null append a fixed explanation — 'the supervisor pane shows no error output (a healthy harness statusline); the supervisor may have bound its socket under a different OVERDECK_HOME' — instead of the '— supervisor output:' suffix. Exact snippet in PRD WI-4. Tests: (a) pane with only a harness statusline → null; (b) pane with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND → error lines returned; (c) thrown timeout message in case (a) contains 'no error output' and does not contain the statusline text.

POST /api/conversations/:name/clear-fork-state operator door guarded on session liveness

expected_outputs: endpoint tests pass: 404 unknown, 409 dead session with no write, 200 live session with cleared fields

narrative.Action: Step 1: add clearConversationFailureState(name) writer to src/lib/overdeck/conversations.ts next to updateForkStatus (line 1411) — one UPDATE setting fork_status/fork_error/spawn_error to NULL (exact SQL in PRD WI-6). Step 2: add handleConversationClearForkState(name) to src/lib/overdeck/conversation-runtime.ts following handleConversationStop (lines 969-985): 404 when getConversationByName misses; 409 with an explanatory error when `await tmuxSessionExists(conv.tmuxSession)` is false (stored failure state is truthful for a dead session); otherwise call the writer and return the updated conversation with sessionAlive: true. Step 3: wire HttpRouter.add('POST', '/api/conversations/:name/clear-fork-state', …) in src/dashboard/server/routes/conversations.ts with the same validateOrigin guard as postConversationStopRoute (lines 327-342) and register the route constant in the module's router aggregation exactly like the other postConversation*Route constants. Tests mock getConversationByName and tmuxSessionExists for the 404/409/200 paths and assert the writer is not called on 409.

pan conversations heal <name> CLI verb via the clear-fork-state endpoint

expected_outputs: heal CLI tests pass: 200 prints cleared line, 409 exits non-zero with guidance, unknown name exits non-zero

narrative.Action: Create src/cli/commands/conversations/heal.ts following move.ts exactly: resolve the conversation by exact name via getConversationByName() (non-zero exit listing candidates on no match), then POST to `${getDashboardApiUrlSync()}/api/conversations/<name>/clear-fork-state`. On 200 print `Cleared fork/spawn failure state for <name> (session alive)`. On 409 print the server error plus guidance: `The tmux session is not alive; the stored failure state is truthful. Use pan conversations show <name> to inspect it.` and exit non-zero. Register the subcommand in registerConversationsCommands() in src/cli/commands/conversations/index.ts alongside the other subcommands. Test in src/cli/commands/conversations/__tests__/heal.test.ts with mocked fetch for the 200/409/unknown paths.

Document the OVERDECK_HOME resolution invariant, degraded-supervisor behavior, and operator door in AGENT-MESSAGE-DELIVERY.md

expected_outputs: docs/AGENT-MESSAGE-DELIVERY.md contains a PAN-3671 section covering the home-resolution invariant, degraded supervisor, and operator door

narrative.Action: Add a short PAN-3671 section to docs/AGENT-MESSAGE-DELIVERY.md (the supervisor socket is already documented at line 14) covering: (1) home-resolution invariant — launcher scripts export OVERDECK_HOME explicitly; the supervisor and in-session pan calls never resolve home from tmux global env; the shared-socket sanitizer pins canonical values and refuses caller-override homes; OVERDECK_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME isolates test instances. (2) Degraded supervisor — a missing socket with a live tmux session is not a spawn failure; delivery proceeds via the channels → tmux-paste fallback with a logged warning. (3) Operator door — POST /api/conversations/:name/clear-fork-state and `pan conversations heal <name>` clear stale fork_status/fork_error/spawn_error when the session is alive; the lifecycle heal clears them automatically on resurrect. Note in the completion that no Mintlify .mdx page covers supervisor sockets, so no user-docs change is needed.
